tldr: Biggest live risk, slightly eased: the levered silver sleeve is still in survivability FAIL territory -- leverage 1.679x vs the signed 1.4x ceiling, and one-action.js is still asking for a >=S$16,600 paydown -- but Friday's silver rally to $61.11 (+3.46%) pushed the stressed margin call ($44.94) to roughly 26.5% away, versus 24.7% on Thursday.

Friday was a genuine broad risk-on rebound, not just a tech bounce: all four major US indices rose together (S&P +0.59%, Nasdaq +0.64%, Dow +0.83%, Russell +0.46%) and VIX fell to 14.84; CNN Fear & Greed snapped back to 45 (Neutral) from Thursday's 38 (Fear) -- but a weak prelim UMich consumer-sentiment print (46.3, a five-month low, current conditions at an all-time low) means the soft-landing story is still two-sided.

Correction to a standing fact that had been feeding this book's rare-earth-basket thesis: the China export-control truce was extended 23 Sep 2026 (Bessent) to 10 Jan 2027, not expiring 10 Nov 2026 as every prior file here assumed -- this removes a near-dated bullish catalyst for MP/Lynas but leaves their DoD-backed, price-floored offtakes untouched.

Gold and silver melted up ALONGSIDE equities Friday (gold +1.52% to $4,220.30, silver +3.46% to $61.11, GDX +2.95%) rather than acting as a hedge -- a repricing toward a less-hawkish Fed path, not classic risk-off demand; Barrick was the lone laggard (-2.33%) on a company-specific 2026 production-guidance cut.

Friday's HK tech rebound (Tencent +3.26%, SMIC +1.50%, Xiaomi +9.72% on a SkyNomad EV order-book beat) was NOT mainland-conviction-driven: Southbound Stock Connect was actually a net SELLER of Xiaomi (-HK$925mn) and SMIC (-HK$261mn) that day, with AIA and Alibaba the real Southbound favorites -- worth knowing before reading the rebound as a China-sentiment signal.
